title: Taiwan Holds National Referendum on Reversing Nuclear Phase-Out, Iraq Reopens Pipeline to Turkey After 12 Years and Seeks Higher OPEC+ Quota, and Turkey Extends Iran Gas Deal to 2032
subhead: Taiwanese voters cast ballots on overturning the island's nuclear energy phase-out to power semiconductor and AI growth, Iraq resumes crude flows through its pipeline to Turkey after a 12-year halt while lobbying OPEC+ for a higher 2027 production ceiling, and Ankara extends its natural gas import contract with Iran by six years through 2032.

sections.heading: Taiwan Votes on Reversing Nuclear Phase-Out for AI Era as Georgia Orders Referendum on $17B Data Center Campus
sections.body:
Voters across Taiwan went to the polls on Saturday in a binding national referendum to decide whether to scrap the ruling Democratic Progressive Party's 'nuclear-free homeland' policy, held alongside local elections for 11,051 municipal officials, Anadolu Agency and Al Jazeera reported. Industry groups and semiconductor executives have warned that without restarting and extending Taiwan's nuclear reactors, the island's power grid cannot reliably sustain the surging electricity demand of advanced chip foundries and artificial intelligence data centers while reducing dependence on imported liquefied natural gas and coal that are vulnerable to a Chinese maritime blockade.

In the United States, grid and land-use backlash against hyperscale computing reached the ballot box after a judge in Coweta County, Georgia, ordered a January 12, 2027 special election allowing voters to repeal the rezoning for Project Sail, a $17 billion data center megaproject spanning more than 800 rural acres southwest of Atlanta, OilPrice reported. Meanwhile in Puerto Rico, thousands of residents joined a 'Day of National Outrage' protest in San Juan against record-high electricity tariffs and chronic grid outages, Al Jazeera noted.
sections.whyItMatters: Taiwan's nuclear referendum and Georgia's special election on a $17 billion data center campus illustrate how the AI power crunch is forcing direct voter referendums on generation mix and grid allocation on both sides of the Pacific.

sections.heading: Iraq Reopens Crude Pipeline to Turkey After 12 Years and Pushes OPEC+ for Higher Quota as Riyadh Blocks US Effort to Fracture Cartel
sections.body:
Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair announced that Baghdad has officially reactivated the Iraq–Türkiye crude oil pipeline after 12 years of inactivity, restoring a vital northern export corridor to the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan just as federal border guards shut unauthorized smuggling crossings in the Kurdistan region, Anadolu Agency and Al Jazeera reported. Ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ ministerial meeting to set 2027 production policy, Khudair confirmed that Iraq is formally negotiating with OPEC for a higher crude production quota to finance domestic energy infrastructure, Reuters and OilPrice reported.

Iraq's quota push comes amid revelations that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman personally intervened earlier this year to halt a quiet diplomatic campaign by the Trump administration encouraging Iraq and Venezuela to consider leaving OPEC, Reuters and The Independent reported. Sources familiar with the talks said Washington had dangled investment and sanctions incentives to weaken the cartel's supply discipline before Riyadh stepped in to preserve OPEC+ cohesion.
sections.whyItMatters: Reopening the Iraq–Türkiye pipeline gives Baghdad additional export capacity precisely as it demands a higher OPEC+ quota, while Saudi Arabia's move to block US efforts to peel Iraq and Venezuela away from OPEC underscores the geopolitical tug-of-war over global spare capacity.

sections.heading: Turkey Extends Iran Natural Gas Import Contract to 2032 and Expands Offshore Oil Footprint Into Guinea-Bissau
sections.body:
Türkiye has extended its long-term natural gas supply agreement with Iran by six years through 2032, securing continued pipeline deliveries to its eastern grid despite intensifying US economic sanctions and maritime blockade pressure on Tehran, Turkish energy officials confirmed. At the same time, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar announced that state oil company TPAO has acquired equity stakes in two offshore exploration blocks in Guinea-Bissau under its strategic partnership with US supermajor Chevron, adding that new upstream deals in Libya are next on Ankara's agenda, Anadolu Agency and Daily Sabah reported.

On the domestic power generation front, Turkish utility Entek Elektrik completed the Ministry of Energy's partial provisional acceptance for the first phase of the Büyükkışla Storage-Integrated Wind Power Plant in Ankara's Şereflikoçhisar district, where 11 of 14 turbines are now built to supply annual electricity equivalent to 83,000 households, industry filings showed.
sections.whyItMatters: By extending Iranian pipeline gas imports to 2032 while simultaneously partnering with Chevron on West African offshore blocks, Ankara is insulating its energy security from Western sanctions blocks and diversifying TPAO into an international upstream operator.

sections.heading: US Navy Disables Blockade-Running Ship and Tankers Hit Mines in Hormuz as Jet Fuel Surge Bankrupts Norse Atlantic
sections.body:
Maritime energy risk escalated sharply in the Persian Gulf after the US military fired disabling shots to knock out the propulsion of a Palau-flagged merchant vessel that departed an Iranian port in defiance of the US blockade, while Iran's IRGC Navy reported that two oil tankers exploded after striking naval mines in unauthorized lanes near the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera, CBS News, and Anadolu Agency reported. Persistent Houthi strikes and Gulf shipping disruptions kept ICE Brent crude near $96 per barrel on Friday, posting a weekly gain that defied earlier Wall Street forecasts of an end-of-year oil glut, OilPrice noted.

The sustained crude and refining premium is triggering acute downstream stress across global aviation and emerging markets. European low-cost long-haul carrier Norse Atlantic Airways filed for bankruptcy protection on Friday after soaring jet fuel costs drained its liquidity, prompting EasyJet CEO Kenton Jarvis to warn that more unhedged airlines could soon collapse, CNBC and OilPrice reported. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia opened cabinet discussions on raising subsidized domestic fuel prices for the first time since 2022 as $96 oil and a weaker rupiah strain the state budget, OilPrice added.
sections.whyItMatters: The bankruptcy of Norse Atlantic and Indonesia's move toward its first subsidized fuel hike in four years show that the $96 oil regime driven by Strait of Hormuz mine strikes and US blockade enforcement is now transmitting real economic damage to transport and fiscal budgets worldwide.

sections.heading: Copper Rallies 6.5% for First Weekly Gain Since October as Congo Disrupts Global Cobalt Supply
sections.body:
Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) surged 6.5% this week to post their first weekly gain in nearly two months, rebounding from a sharp autumn correction that followed September's all-time high above $15,000 per metric ton, OilPrice reported. Traders cited tightening exchange inventories and renewed industrial restocking ahead of 2027 grid and defense manufacturing orders.

Meanwhile, regulatory and export disruptions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)—which accounts for more than 70% of global mined output—rattled the international market for cobalt, a critical mineral essential for high-density aerospace batteries, defense electronics, and electric vehicles, Industrial Info Resources reported, as mining planners also flagged project delays ahead of the upcoming Future Minerals Forum.
sections.whyItMatters: Copper's 6.5% rebound and fresh cobalt supply friction in the DRC underscore that industrial and battery metal markets remain structurally tight despite macro volatility, keeping input costs elevated for grid expansion and defense manufacturing.

bottomLine: Taiwan's national referendum on reviving nuclear power, Iraq's reopening of its northern oil pipeline to Türkiye alongside a push for a higher OPEC+ quota, and Ankara's six-year extension of Iranian gas imports to 2032 demonstrate how states are locking in physical baseload power and pipeline corridors while Gulf blockade warfare and $96 crude force airline bankruptcies and fuel subsidy cuts.
sources: Anadolu Agency, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OilPrice, CNBC, CBS News, The Independent, Daily Sabah, and Industrial Info Resources.
